listing.name: Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter + Balance of Power (OpenXvT)
listing.summary: A native engine for X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter with your own Balance of Power game data.
listing.original_game_title: Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter + Balance of Power

steps.title: Choose your original game data
steps.instruction: Select your complete X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter installation root containing BalanceOfPower. The base game by itself is insufficient.

steps.title: Start the Linux player
steps.instruction: Extract the upstream v0.0.5 linux-x86_64-release.tar.xz yourself. Keep the resources, shaders and lib folder beside OpenXvT. Run OpenXvT with glibc 2.35 or later and a Vulkan driver. The OpenXvT build also needs libcurl.so.4.

warnings: Back up the entire effective profile, all original game folders, and the working player before updating. If the profile cannot be opened, check the working directory for pilots, settings and other files.

references.title: Open the Apple silicon Mac app
references.instruction: Mount the upstream v0.0.5 macos-arm64-release.dmg and copy OpenXvT.app out of it. Use Apple silicon, macOS 13 or later and Metal. Keep the app bundle intact and maintain this copy outside Portcove.

references.title: Keep your settings and pilots
references.instruction: The normal SDL profile is TotallyOpen/OpenXvT under the Linux data home or Mac Application Support. Keep the whole profile with the player closed.

presentation.manual_preparation: On Play, keep the normal in-process setup picker and select your own complete X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter installation with its BalanceOfPower subfolder. Balance of Power is required by this implementation; the base game alone is not the offered tuple. Keep the full original root, package resources, DLLs, shaders and established control/music choices. Optional explicit setup/import arguments are upstream tools, not forced on each start. Multiplayer and save compatibility have not been qualified here. Normal user settings, pilots, replays and temporary files belong to the current account’s SDL preference directory TotallyOpen/OpenXvT; preserve that WHOLE effective profile and every original-data root. Config defaults inside resources are immutable package files, separate from user config.yaml. Core manages only the engine and the listed local config files, not shared external profiles. If SDL profile lookup fails, user/temporary output can fall back to the executable working directory. Arbitrarily named pilots, replays and cache/temp files there are unclaimed modified-runtime data: existing guards refuse destructive maintenance while retaining the creating runtime. A Core backup of declared files does not back up those unknown files. Preserve the WHOLE creating runtime and all effective profiles before reviewing recovery; do not delete files to force an update or assume re-download repairs saves. No automatic migration, portable-pilot backup, backward-save conversion or automatic recovery is offered.
